attributes.bears: roll number, route, season, and the Wardenry's stamp struck through the glaze
attributes.carried_by: the master of the crossing, on a thong at the neck — never left in a wagon, never handed to a hand
attributes.if_it_is_broken_at_the_centre: Ysoly's tile and Iseul Fane's rank are the same instrument seen from two ends. Iseul is the only Warden of the Third Rank between the rims while this crossing is out; she is therefore the only person who can declare the hazard, and the only person who can lawfully break the tile that would start the clock against it. Both acts are spoken aloud, on the ground, in front of witnesses, and they are seconds apart in either order. Written down, the whole of chapter 5 is a question of sequence: if the requirement is spoken over a whole tile it is on the roll and survives everything after; if the clay goes first there was never a licence-holder standing there. There is no appeal on the plain and no other tile within three hundred and eighty-five miles.
attributes.legal_basis: the Second Article of the Roadwarden Statute — no wagon, beast or person passes the bounds unlicensed; the tile is the licence, and the same Article that creates it grants the power to break it. Its weight in chapter 5 comes from elsewhere: the fourth proviso of the Fourth Article, which gives a whole tile a clock.
attributes.material: fired clay, salt-ash glaze, about four inches square, heavier than it looks
attributes.revocation: Granted in the text: the Second Article lets a Warden of the Third Rank or above revoke on the road by breaking the tile in the holder's hand and in his sight. The cause is spoken before the break, before one witness who can be named; the halves are kept and carried back to the roll at Bell Harrow and the cause entered beside the roll number. Below the Third Rank a Warden may take a tile up and report it and may not break it — which at the centre means one person on the plain can do this, and she is the same person the Fourth Article needs. The master may sue the cause at the rim and be paid his loss if it fails. He does not get the crossing back. The tile is not mended and the season is gone.
attributes.the_lever: Under the fourth proviso of the Fourth Article, the master of a lawful crossing standing on sealed ground with his tile whole may require the hazard survey be begun before the turn of the next season, and the Warden must enter that requirement on the roll beside the seal. It is the only clock that runs against a seal. Break the tile before the requirement is spoken and the demand dies with it: no licence, no standing, no clock, and the ground is held the way Ferrant's ground has been held for fourteen years. Break it after and the requirement stands — the Article says so in as many words, because the men who wrote the proviso could see that far and no further.
attributes.who_holds_one: Ysoly Tamm — one current tile, stamped for the centre route

name: The Crossing Licence Tile
summary: A fired clay tile the size of a palm, glazed white with salt-ash and stamped through with the Wardenry's roll number, the route and the season it is good for. The caravan master carries it on a thong at the neck and surrenders it at the far rim; an unbroken tile is a lawful crossing and a broken tile is no crossing at all. A Warden of the Third Rank or above revokes by speaking the cause and then breaking the tile in the holder's hand, in front of them, which is why every master on the plain flinches at the sound of fired clay.
